messages:
jess_lin: FYI — Lyra Health (dedicated pool) is seeing intermittent 429s and tail latency spikes during today's marketing campaign. They say baseline QPS ~120, but we observed sustained bursts up to ~920 QPS for ~8m. They hit throttles and some 5xx. Can we triage?

samir_k: Noted. Pool id? configs? any autoscale events logged? :eyes:

jess_lin: pool_id: ded-lyra-02. Config from console: GPUs=4xA100-40GB (min=4, max=12), autoscale.cooldown=60s, scale_up_step=1, target_util=0.7. Customer had prefix caching disabled (disable_cache=true) in client.

alex_cheng: Quick logs from proxy showing rate limits: `{"status":429,"error":"rate_limit","detail":"pool_throttle"}` and a few `503` from runtime while scale-up was in flight. Latency graph: 95p went from ~120ms -> 2.1s at peak.

maria_ops: incidents-bot shows spikes starting 2026-03-15T09:18Z and scale events at 09:19Z and 09:20Z but pool was still at 4 GPUs through most of the surge. Autoscaler took ~45-70s to add nodes, and scale_up_step=1 meant we only added one GPU at a time.

samir_k: That matches a classic ramp/overshoot. With target_util 0.7 and sudden 900 QPS, 4 GPUs are insufficient. Two immediate things: 1) noisy-neighbor unlikely (dedicated pool) but scheduler placement can cause CPU+IO contention; 2) autoscale config too conservative for marketing bursts.

jess_lin: Customer timeline: they started a campaign at 09:15, QPS rose quickly. They sent a repro curl that hit ~140 concurrent connections. I'll paste the repro they tried: ```bash
for i in {1..140}; do curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/completions \
  -H \"Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_KEY\" \
  -H \"Content-Type: application/json\" \
  -d '{"model":"llm-large","prompt":"hi","max_tokens":32}' &
done
wait
```

alex_cheng: Repro is good — generates a massive cold-KV-cache pressure and many requests require full attention. Also they passed `disable_cache=true` which blocks our prefix cache; that increases per-token work.

samir_k: Suggested mitigations: increase min GPUs to 8 for campaign windows OR temporarily bump scale_up_step to 3 and reduce cooldown to 15s. Also enable prefix/KV cache (remove disable_cache) and add a smaller model fallback for non-critical traffic.

jess_lin: Lyra asked for quick fix without infra changes. Any short-term control we can apply from our side?

maria_ops: We can apply a burst_capacity override for pool ded-lyra-02 — allocate N tokens/sec headroom (e.g., +2000 tok/s) to avoid 429s while autoscaler catches up. But this consumes credits; sales needs to sign off if it's a bill-impacting change.

samir_k: Also we can tweak routing policy: send non-latency-sensitive endpoints to a cheaper model variant `llm-medium` during campaign. That is a config change (route-level). Lower tokens/sec per request.

alex_cheng: Pulled `rbxctl pool describe ded-lyra-02` — snippet: ```
POOL_ID: ded-lyra-02
GPUS: 4 x A100-40GB
AUTOSCALE: min=4 max=12 step=1 cooldown=60s target_util=0.7
CURRENT_LOAD: baseline_qps=120 peak_qps=920 observed_avg_util=0.88
RECENT_EVENTS:
 - 09:18:12 scaleup requested
 - 09:19:00 scaleup completed (added 1 gpu)
 - 09:20:05 scaleup completed (added 1 gpu)
```

jess_lin: They reported some 5xxs with message "runtime oom" — could be per-GPU memory pressure when many simultaneous sequences allocate KV cache.

samir_k: If memory OOM, options: reduce max_tokens or use quantized model variant (q4) for campaign, or add GPUs. We should check per-GPU VRAM usage timeline. Can anyone pull `metrics.vram` for that window?

alex_cheng: Grabbed VRAM timeline — shows spikes to ~95% on GPU0 during peak, others at ~70-85%. So load wasn't evenly distributed. Possibly uneven routing or KV hot-shard.

maria_ops: Action items: 1) Ask Lyra to re-enable prefix caching (they intentionally disabled for dedup reasons) — if they can't, 2) offer to temporarily raise min GPUs to 8 for campaign window, 3) change autoscale to step=3 cooldown=15s for aggressive ramp, 4) enable model fallback routing. Who's on owner?

jess_lin: I'll own customer comms and get permission for config changes. Can eng ops do a one-off scale/config change pending approval?

samir_k: I can push a temporary config: set autoscale.step=3 cooldown=15s and bump min=6 as a conservative step, plus set burst_capacity=2000 for ded-lyra-02. Will schedule change in 10m pending sign-off.

support-bot: Deploy job queued: change-autoscale(ded-lyra-02) by samir_k — CI checks passed. ETA 2m. :rocket:

incidents-bot: Alert suppressed for ded-lyra-02 for 30m per on-call manual ack by maria_ops.

jess_lin: Customer approved temporary changes. I'll monitor and report back after next campaign window. Thanks all. :thumbsup:

samir_k: Follow-ups: we should schedule a postmortem with Lyra to set utilization targets (we recommend 50-60% sustained for marketing bursts) and plan guaranteed burst pools for future campaigns. Also recommend they enable prefix caching for the campaign.

alex_cheng: I'll capture graphs and put a short runbook in /docs/support/lyra-dedicated-runbook (private) with repro commands and config snippets.

maria_ops: Noted — tagging sales to discuss cost/contract for guaranteed burst capacity.

jess_lin: Closing loop later today with result summary.
